Empirical Research Plan:  “Does temporary financial scarcity impair cognition and self-control?  Evidence from Indian sugarcane farmers”

======================================================================
1. Identification Strategy
----------------------------------------------------------------------
Strategy:  Event-study Difference-in-Differences (DID) with individual
fixed effects that exploits the fact that each farmer is observed
multiple times at known distances from his/her own harvest date.

Why it fits
• Harvest generates a large, predictable, and highly idiosyncratic cash
  shock.  
• The order in which plots are harvested is set by the sugar mill’s
  quota schedule, which is plausibly exogenous to farmers’ short-run
  cognition.  
• Because all farmers experience both “low-cash” (before harvest) and
  “high-cash” (after harvest) periods, we can difference **within the
  same person**, eliminating all time-invariant unobservables.  
• Including farmers who are pre-harvest and post-harvest in the *same
  calendar week* gives us a second DID dimension that removes common
  seasonal shocks.

Mathematically,

Y_{it} = Σ_{k≠–1} β_k·1{days_since_harvest = k}_it  + γ_i + δ_week(t)
         + X′_{it}θ + ε_{it}

where week fixed effects δ remove calendar-time shocks and farmer
fixed effects γ remove time-invariant farmer heterogeneity.

======================================================================
2. Treatment and Control
----------------------------------------------------------------------
• Treatment variable  
  Scarcity_it = 1 if farmer i is *pre-harvest* (days_since_harvest < 0),
  0 if *post-harvest* (days_since_harvest ≥ 0).

• Control group  
  Same farmer observed post-harvest provides the counterfactual.  At any
  calendar week we can also use other farmers who have already
  harvested as additional controls.

• Treatment timing / event date  
  Event date = individual harvest day (t = 0).  We observe farmers at
  t = {–60, –30, –7, 0, +7, +30, +60} days.

• No running variable needed (not an RDD), but we will show an event-time
  plot.

======================================================================
3. Key Identifying Assumptions
----------------------------------------------------------------------
A1.  Conditional Parallel Trends  
     In the absence of the liquidity shock, cognition for pre- and
     post-harvest farmers in the same calendar week would follow the
     same trend.  Plausibility: high, because the only difference is
     cash-on-hand; weather, pests, and labor supply are shared locally
     and week fixed effects absorb them.

A2.  Exogenous Harvest Timing  
     Mill cutting order is set before the season and not revised for
     short-run farmer behavior.  Farmers cannot strategically time
     their cognitive test to coincide with liquidity.  Backed by mill
     records and interviews.

A3.  No Differential Learning / Fatigue  
     Repeated cognitive tests could generate learning; we minimize this
     by using alternate Raven matrices and randomizing test order.

A4.  SUTVA  
     One farmer’s harvest does not affect another’s cognition (no
     spillovers), reasonable because cash windfall is idiosyncratic and
     tests are individual.

======================================================================
4. Threats to Identification & Mitigations
----------------------------------------------------------------------
T1. Seasonality (rainfall, temperature) could co-move with harvest.  
    → Include week-of-year fixed effects and village × week controls;
      restrict analysis to a ±60-day window.

T2. Endogenous attrition: post-harvest farmers might be away selling
    cane and unavailable for testing.  
    → Offer home visits at flexible times and record missingness; test
      for differential attrition with logit on observables; bound
      estimates with Lee bounds.

T3. Test-retest effects (learning).  
    → Counterbalance order, use different but psychometrically
      equivalent forms, include “placebo” outcomes such as height to
      show no mechanical score drift.

======================================================================
5. R Code Outline
----------------------------------------------------------------------
```r
# 0. Packages ---------------------------------------------------------
library(data.table)   # fast data handling
library(fixest)       # high-dimensional FE regressions
library(lmtest)       # coeftest for cluster-robust SEs
library(sandwich)     # vcovHC

# 1. Load Data --------------------------------------------------------
dt <- fread("sugarcane_cognition_panel.csv")  # one row per person-wave

# 2. Construct Variables ---------------------------------------------
# days_since_harvest already included (negative = pre, positive = post)
dt[, scarcity := as.integer(days_since_harvest < 0)]

# Event-time dummies for ±60 days (omit –1 as baseline)
event_window <- -60:60
for(k in event_window){
  if(k != -1){
    dt[, paste0("d",k) := as.integer(days_since_harvest == k)]
  }
}

# 3. Main Specification ----------------------------------------------
fe_formula <- as.formula(
  paste("cog_score ~",
        paste(paste0("d", event_window[event_window != -1]), collapse = " + "),
        "| farmer_id + week_year")
)
est_main <- feols(fe_formula, data = dt, cluster = ~farmer_id)
summary(est_main)

# 4. Simple pre/post DID for interpretability ------------------------
est_did <- feols(cog_score ~ scarcity | farmer_id + week_year,
                 data = dt, cluster = ~farmer_id)
summary(est_did)

# 5. Robustness:   Tight window (±30 days) ----------------------------
dt30 <- dt[abs(days_since_harvest) <= 30]
est_30 <- feols(cog_score ~ scarcity | farmer_id + week_year,
                data = dt30, cluster = ~farmer_id)
summary(est_30)

# 6. Robustness:  Add weather controls -------------------------------
est_weather <- feols(cog_score ~ scarcity + temp + rainfall |
                     farmer_id + week_year,
                     data = dt, cluster = ~farmer_id)
summary(est_weather)
```

======================================================================
6. Expected Results
----------------------------------------------------------------------
Prior: scarcity (pre-harvest) lowers fluid intelligence by roughly
0.15–0.20 SD and raises impulsive choices (present bias) by about
5–10 p.p.  Direction: negative for cognition, positive for self-control
failures.

======================================================================
7. Validity Checklist Self-Assessment (Difference-in-Differences)
----------------------------------------------------------------------
C1: Parallel trends visually supported by event-study pre-trends ..... 1  
C2: No simultaneous confounders (week FE + same farmers) ............. 1  
C3: Exogeneity of treatment timing (mill schedule) ................... 1  
C4: Stable composition / attrition minimal and tested ................ 0.5  
C5: No interference or spillovers among units ........................ 0.5  
TOTAL (out of 5) .................................................... 4.0

======================================================================
End of Plan
